role_hint: Operators can upload ISOs and start installs, but cannot change users, mail, network or updates.
sign_in_sub: Manage the boot server for your network.
forgot_sub: Enter your username or email. If it is known, you receive a link to choose a new password.
forgot_nomail: No mail server is set up yet, so passwords cannot be reset by email. Ask an administrator to reset it in Users.
reset_sent: If the account exists, a reset link is on its way.
reset_done: Password changed. You can sign in now.
err_reset: This link has expired or the passwords do not match.
err_password: Passwords do not match, are shorter than 8 characters, or the current password is wrong.
mail_reset_subject: Reset your PXE Boot Server password
mail_reset_body: Someone asked to reset the password of your account. Use the link below within an hour. If it was not you, ignore this email.
setup_sub: Create the first administrator account. After this you choose the network clients boot from.
dash_sub: Everything a client needs to boot from the network, at a glance.
dash_setup_network: Choose the network interface clients boot from before you start.
st1d: The client asks the network for a boot file. Your router keeps handing out IP addresses.
st2d: undionly.kpxe (Legacy BIOS) or ipxe.efi (UEFI) over TFTP.
st3d: The ISO menu is fetched over HTTP. Folders become submenus.
st4d: Windows via wimboot, Linux via kernel and initrd, anything else via sanboot.
live_sub: Clients that are booting or installing right now: which ISO, which step and how far along.
nolive: No clients are booting right now.
nolive_sub: Clients appear here as soon as they load the boot menu.
live_note: Progress comes from the server: bytes sent over HTTP for boot files, files read over the Windows share during setup, and the answer file being fetched. The server cannot look inside an installer, so during installation it shows activity rather than a percentage. Unattended installs report back when they are finished.
stats_sub: Bandwidth and running tasks on this server, updated every second.
lib_sub: Upload ISO files and sort them in folders. Every ISO is detected and added to the boot menu automatically. Files copied straight into the ISO directory show up after a rescan.
drop_t: Drop ISO files here or click to browse
drop_d: Large files are sent in 32 MB pieces. If the connection drops, the upload continues where it stopped.
folder_name: Folder name, e.g. Windows or Linux/Ubuntu
no_isos_sub: Upload an ISO above to get started.
bm_sub: This is what a client sees on screen after it starts from the network.
bm_preview_note: Folders open as submenus. Use the arrow keys and Enter on the client.
ans_sub: Install Linux and Proxmox without questions. Build an answer file with the wizard, link it to an ISO and it gets its own entry in the boot menu.
no_answers_sub: Create one for an Ubuntu, Debian, Rocky/Alma or Proxmox ISO.
ans_note: An unattended entry wipes the chosen disk without asking. Link it to a machine with "Next boot only" to install exactly once.
wiz_sub: Six short steps. The file on the right updates while you type.
no_linux_isos_sub: Answer files work with Ubuntu Server, Debian, Rocky, Alma, Fedora and Proxmox VE ISOs. Upload one first.
w_host_hint: A machine linked in Machines uses its own name as hostname instead.
w_hint_pw: Passwords are stored as a SHA-512 hash, never in plain text.
pw_unchanged: Leave empty to keep the current one
w_wipe_warn: Machines that boot this entry are installed without any question, and the chosen disk is wiped.
w_wipe: I understand the chosen disk is wiped without asking
answer_saved: Answer file saved. The boot menu has a new unattended entry.
err_confirm_wipe: Confirm that the disk may be wiped.
err_answer_iso: This ISO does not support answer files.
m_sub: Link a MAC address to an ISO, with or without an answer file. That machine then skips the menu and starts straight away.
m_name_hint: Also used as hostname in unattended installs.
mo_once_d: Afterwards the machine gets the normal menu again, so it never reinstalls in a loop.
mo_always_d: For kiosks and test machines that should always start this ISO.
mo_default_d: Shows the menu with this ISO as the default choice.
no_machines_sub: Link a MAC address from the boot log or enter one yourself.
machine_saved: Machine linked. It uses this setting on its next network boot.
err_mac: Enter a MAC address like aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff.
log_sub: Every client that loads the boot menu, with what it chose.
net_sub: Choose how this server answers PXE requests. Proxy mode works next to your existing DHCP server, such as a UniFi gateway.
welcome_network: Account created. Now choose the network interface clients boot from and click Apply.
iface_hint: PXE answers go out on every interface you tick. Add a VLAN interface below to serve another VLAN.
serverip_hint: Leave empty to use the address of the first ticked interface.
uefi_ipxe: built-in drivers for most network cards
uefi_snp: uses the firmware's network driver, most compatible
m_proxy_d: Your router keeps handing out addresses. This server only adds the boot information.
m_full_d: For an isolated install network or DHCP relay. Hands out addresses itself.
secureboot: Turn off Secure Boot on clients: iPXE and wimboot are not signed by Microsoft.
network_applied: Network settings applied. dnsmasq has restarted.
vlan_add_sub: Lets this server answer PXE requests inside another VLAN. The switch port must carry that VLAN tagged.
vlan_addr_hint: Static address with prefix, for example 10.0.50.5/24. Leave empty to use DHCP.
err_vlan: Check the VLAN ID (1-4094) and the address.
confirm_vlan_del: Remove VLAN interface {name}? Clients in that VLAN can no longer boot from this server.
users_sub: People who can sign in to manage this server.
err_user: Could not save the user. The username may exist already, or the password is shorter than 8 characters.
mail_sub: Used for password resets and notifications, such as a finished upload or install.
notify_upload: When an ISO upload has finished
notify_install: When an unattended install has finished
mail_test_subject: Test email from PXE Boot Server
mail_test_body: The mail settings work. You will receive password resets and notifications at this address.
set_sub: General settings and your own account.
iso_dir_hint: You can also copy ISO files here directly (for example with scp), then click Rescan in the library.
smb_sub: Windows setup connects to the share with a password that is generated on install. Rotate it if you think it leaked.
confirm_smb: Generate a new share password? Windows installs that are running right now may lose their connection.
help_sub: How the server works, how to use it across VLANs and what to do when a client does not boot.
js_uptodate: You are on the latest version.
js_updating: Updating. The web interface restarts when it is done.
js_update_failed: The update failed. The previous version is still running; see the log above.
js_confirm_delete_iso: Delete {name}? The ISO file is removed from the server.
js_nolive: No clients are booting right now.
js_up_reselect: Paused. Choose the same file again to continue.
js_up_exists: A file with this name already exists in this folder.
js_folder_invalid: Use letters, numbers, spaces, dots and dashes in folder names.
js_folder_not_empty: Only empty folders can be deleted.
js_move_failed: Could not move the ISO. A file with that name may already be in the folder.
js_menu_timeout: Starts the default entry after {n} seconds
js_mail_no_to: Enter an address to send the test email to.
